524	## 5. Loop configuration
525	
526	**Read `## 5.0 Verification standard` (added 2026-09-19, right after this table) before running
527	any of the remaining rows (3.6 onward).** It's a cross-cutting addition earned the hard way during
528	the post-commit-11 ad hoc pass — six real, shipped defects slipped past this table's own
529	per-step checks the first time through, all for the same handful of reasons. The per-step checks
530	below are unchanged and still the specific thing being tested; §5.0 is what makes sure they're
531	actually being *proven*, not just read off the source and assumed.
532	
533	| Step | Tester checks | Scorer PASS gate |
534	|---|---|---|
535	| **0** | Nothing to drive. Read `detect-changes`'s output on the first cart PR after merge. | `e2e_scope == cart` on a cart-only PR; `homepage` still resolves for a homepage-only PR; zero-spec `--grep "@cart"` run reports "no tests found" and exits 0. |
536	| **1.1** | Resolve `xLarge` at 1440 and 1920 viewport widths. Confirm 1186px both times, not 1180.8 and 1574. Confirm the five other size variants byte-identical. | 1186px rem constant at both widths; `maxWidth: '100%'` present; five sibling variants unchanged; `grep` for `xLarge` consumers still returns only the type union and the story. |
537	| **1.2** | Drive the drawer: open, Escape, backdrop click, close button. Tab through and confirm focus never escapes the panel. Close and confirm focus returns to the trigger **and** scroll position is where it was. Render empty and confirm the 52px band is still occupying space. Resize 1920 → 1440 → 834 → 402 and confirm two-column → single-column at tablet with a 32px gutter. | All four close paths call `onClose`; `finalFocusRef` receives focus; scroll offset restored (not just unlocked); `min-height` on the messages band equals the 52px token in the empty story; single-column at and below tablet; `659.2` appears nowhere; `recipeParts` and `recipeGuards` green; recipe registered. |
538	| **2.1** | This is the one step the Tester cannot score alone. Confirm all eight markers log in the running app **from three surfaces**: the cart, the account wishlist page, and a checkout summary. | Eight files, `.tsx`, `tsc` clean, zero logic diff from base, `item-variant` imports relative not base-path, markers observed on all three surfaces, **Marcel's explicit go-ahead recorded** before step 2.2 starts. |
539	| **2.2** | Pass a `width` and an `mr` to `CartItemVariantImage` from a test caller and confirm the caller wins. Pass a `color` to `CartItemVariantName` and confirm it applies. Render with no stepper and no actions. Render at 402px and look for any truncation or hidden element. | Caller-props win on image and name; gift-card render emits neither slot and throws nothing; colour+size is one text node; no array shorthand in geometry; `audit:tokens` clean; `recipeGuards` confirms `Zimm*` namespacing on both recipes. |
540	| **3.1** | Drive the stepper through all five quantity conditions: 1, 2, at-max, fully-OOS, unavailable. Keyboard only: Tab to each control, Enter and Space. Confirm the focus ring is visibly different from rest. | Five states each assert the right enabled/disabled pair and the 0.4 opacity where greyed; keyboard operable; `aria-label` on both; focus-visible resolved value ≠ default; resolved target ≥24×24; `play` covers increment/decrement/boundary. |
541	| **3.2** | Render each of the three copy strings. Confirm DOM position between stepper and actions. Confirm error state widens the details gap. | Three strings verbatim; error → `status.error` token, warning → `text.muted` token; gap 12 → 16 on error; no hex literals; no low-stock variant in the union. |
542	| **3.3** | Render on-sale with quantity 2 and confirm both Was and Now scale. Render with and without a discount label. | Was struck, Now current, both quantity-scaled; label present only when the prop is; no `display-price` override created. |
543	| **3.4** | Feed the mapper a full line item, one with no image, one with missing colour, one with `c_maxOrderQuantity` absent, one with it set to 5, one with it set to `"abc"`. | Fallback returns 3 on absent/0/negative/non-numeric; returns 5 when set to 5; mapper emits one combined colour+size string; `grep` finds no SDK hook in any leaf; `product-detail/index.tsx` unmodified. |
544	| **3.6** (this row was still labeled 3.5 here after the 2026-09-18 renumbering — see the Commit order table and §4's own step heading, both correctly say 3.6; fixed 2026-09-19, found by the Tester dispatched for this exact step) | Run Storybook's a11y check on every story in B3. Then keyboard-only through a full cart item: image → name → price → stepper − → stepper + → message → Remove → Move to Wishlist. | 11 ACs each mapped in the PR body to a file and an assertion; a11y check green on every story; live region preserved (as of 2026-09-19, this step's own Scorer found the real mechanism is `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s own `aria-live="polite"` value span, not `product-quantity-picker.tsx`'s now-orphaned `VisuallyHidden role="status"` — see §4's step 3.6 text); no colour-only state. |
545	| **4.1** | Mock passwordless success and assert the merge. Mock create-account and assert no merge. Then run the existing suites for `header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu` and `product-view`. | `mergeBasket` once, `sum_quantities`, `createDestinationBasket: true`; not called on register; social route untouched; all four consumers' suites green; hook signature unchanged; blast radius named in the PR body. |
546	| **4.2** | **Adversarial pass — the only step that gets one.** Try to make it double-write: fire the callback and the render guard simultaneously. Fire twice on the same basket version. Make the server reject and confirm it stops. Drive the boundary at 2, 3, 4, 5. Then assert call **order**, not just end state. | One write under concurrency; one write per basket version; server rejection surfaces an error with no retry storm; `>=` boundary correct at 3 and 4; consolidation to one line at 3; merge → cap → resume order asserted; `useIsMutating()` no-op proven by making it fail on purpose first. |
547	| **4.3** | Emit each of the three messages. Confirm one emit site by grep. | One emit site; three strings verbatim; SFCC-404 marker present. The `within(document.body)`/portal-exception criterion is deferred to whichever of step 4.4/4.6 first renders a message-triggering component — see step 4.3's own pass criterion 3 text (corrected 2026-09-20) for why a hook-only step can't meet it. |
548	| **4.4** | Remove at qty 1 and qty 3. Wishlist-move at qty 1 and qty 3. Already-in-wishlist. Guest click. Guest completes email-code. Guest completes a simulated redirect. A 6-minute-old pending item. Keyboard-only on both links, checking the focus ring. | One call for a qty-3 remove (not three); single SKU saved on a qty-3 move; count decrements by full quantity; item stays in cart on already-in-wishlist and on guest click; resume works from state **and** from storage; stale item not resumed and both stores cleared; focus-visible ≠ default on both links. |
549	| **4.5** | Remove the last item. Confirm the discrete component renders and the header text changes at the same moment. Render at a non-AU site and inspect the CTA href. | Discrete component (no inline JSX); header and body both switch; CTA href site-prefixed; two-to-one collapse asserted; no hardcoded AU contact details. |
550	| **5.1** | Render domestic and count children. Render international and assert Apple Pay is absent from the DOM, then measure group height against domestic-minus-express. Drive hover/focus/active/disabled on all three buttons. Click Checkout domestic; click it as an international guest and as an international authenticated shopper. | Three children domestic in fixed order; **one** child international with `queryByRole` null and height unchanged; all five states asserted per button with focus-visible ≠ default; h52/px32/gap16 resolved from `actionSizes` tokens not literals; error story renders enabled with zero feedback copy; both international branches reach the stub; `countries.ts` unmodified. |
551	| **4.6** (inserted 2026-09-20, built after 5.1 — see its own step text for why the label doesn't match build order) | Render with a real multi-line basket and confirm one `ProductItem` per line via `cartItemMapper`'s own output. Force a basket over the cap and confirm the render guard fires exactly once and no-ops while a mutation is in flight. Click each item's Remove/Wishlist links and confirm the real mutations fire, not a stub. Render with zero items and confirm `ZimmCartEmptyState`, not an empty list. | One `ProductItem` per line, mapped not hand-built; render guard proven to run and to no-op under `useIsMutating()`, mirroring 4.2's own proof but for the real wiring; `secondaryActions` is a real `ZimmCartItemActions` on every item; empty state swaps in at zero items; `footer`/`messages` slots render `ZimmCartButtonGroup`/`useCartMessages` output; container owns no `isOpen`/`onClose` state itself; exactly one production `<ZimmCartDrawer` call site. |
552	
553	---
554	
555	## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)
556	
557	Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
558	by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
559	Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
560	mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
561	dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
562	each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.
563	
564	1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
565	   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
566	   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
567	   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
568	   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
569	   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
570	2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
571	   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
572	   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
573	   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
574	   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
575	   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
576	   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
577	   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
578	3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
579	   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
580	   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
581	   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
582	   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
583	4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
584	   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
585	   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
586	   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
587	5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
588	   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
589	   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
590	   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
591	6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
592	   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
593	   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
594	   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
595	7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
596	   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
597	   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
598	   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
599	   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
600	8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
601	   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
602	   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.
603	
604	## 6. Open questions
605	
606	These block the handoff. None is a decision I should make for you.
607	
608	1. **`.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 and owner approval is not confirmed.** B0 is BLOCKED until either the authenticated `gh` login is verified in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or a named approving review is secured. Until B0 lands, every cart PR gets `e2e_scope: skip` and no PR-time E2E.
609	
610	2. **`overrides/app/components/item-variant/` has no CODEOWNERS entry and there is no catch-all.** Five files with an 11-surface blast radius would merge with **no required reviewer**. Adding the entry is a Tier 1 Governance change to `CODEOWNERS`, explicitly outside my scope. Your call: add it as a separate ticket first, or accept that the widest-reaching part of this change is ungoverned and compensate with a manually-requested reviewer on B2.
611	
612	3. **`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` is also ungoverned, and the merge call changes auth behaviour for three surfaces outside the cart** (`header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view`). Not in `frozenFiles.md`, not in `protectedFiles.md`'s shared-hooks list, no CODEOWNERS entry. This is a second instance of #2 and arguably the more dangerous one. Does B4 need an explicitly requested reviewer, and does the cross-surface behaviour change need Hard Rule #10 scope confirmation from you before it is written?
613	
614	4. **`overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` does not exist.** The settled decision says "use `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts`, not the base hook" — but that file is absent, and the path is listed in `protectedFiles.md` and routed in CODEOWNERS to `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b @tier-2-approvers @tier-1-approvers`. So honouring the decision literally means **creating a Tier 2 shared hook** this bundle has not budgeted a review for. My recommendation: import the base hook at `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast` and wrap it in our own untiered `useCartMessages.ts`. That satisfies the decision's actual intent (one handler, SFCC-404 is a one-file swap), costs no Tier 2 review, and automatically picks up the override the day someone creates it. I have **not** applied this — the decision is yours to confirm.
615	
616	5. **The stepper's `+` and `−` are a mismatched pair.** `MinusIcon` is a Zimmermann/Figma icon in `overrides/app/components/icons/zimm.tsx`; `PlusIcon` is re-exported from the base template in `index.tsx`. That file's own comments show the established pattern of migrating an icon into `zimm.tsx` when the base glyph is wrong (`CloseIcon`: "off-centre glyph within its viewBox"; the chevrons: filled vs stroked). AGENTS.md is explicit: if a required icon is missing from the overrides set, **ask — do not substitute a visually different one**. Is the base `PlusIcon` acceptable against Figma's `Icon_plus`, or does it need adding to `zimm.tsx`?
617	
618	6. **Apple Pay and Google Pay marks do not exist.** `zimm.tsx` has `ZimmAppleSignInIcon` and `ZimmGoogleSignInIcon` — sign-in marks, not Pay marks — and there is no `applePay`/`googlePay` asset anywhere in `overrides/app`. Both are brand-licensed artwork with usage rules. SFCC-275 AC1 requires 48×24 logos. Same AGENTS.md rule applies: ask, do not substitute. This is the only part of B5 that cannot pass.
619	
620	7. **Nothing opens the cart drawer, and no story owns the trigger.** See the closing line.
621	
622	8. **Container placement needs your confirmation.** SFCC-271's mutations and SFCC-250's guards need something that owns `useCurrentBasket()`, and `components.md` forbids data-fetching in anything under `overrides/app/components/`. Base `pages/cart/index.jsx` exists, so the override rule would normally say copy-first it — but the session notes decided 315 is explicitly "not an override of base `pages/cart`". My plan threads this by creating a **new custom file** at `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (a path CODEOWNERS already routes to `@pwa-squad-a`, Tier 3), leaving base `pages/cart/index.jsx` untouched and still serving `/cart` as today — a sibling file named anything other than `index` does not shadow the base page. ## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)

Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.

1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.

**Claim:** "the header bag `IconButton` at `header/rightBar/index.tsx:418` has **no `onClick` and no
`to`/`href`** — it is a dead button today."

**That is false.** The element spans ~418–437 and carries `onClick={onMyCartClick}` at **line 436**.
The planner read the opening tag and stopped before the handler.

**But the underlying concern is real, and sharper than the planner's version.** Traced through:

```
header/rightBar/index.tsx:436   onClick={onMyCartClick}
header/index.tsx:252            onMyCartClick={onMyCartClick}
_app/index.tsx:422              onMyCartClick={onCartClick}

The bag button **navigates to the `/cart` route**. It does not open a drawer. `/cart` renders base
`pages/cart/index.jsx`.

**So SFCC-315's drawer has no trigger. Nothing in the app opens it.** The bundle can ship all seven
stories fully complete and no shopper will ever see the drawer.

Re-verified: no CODEOWNERS entry, and no catch-all rule exists in the file.

The planner's catch, not in the session notes. Every branch adding a recipe must register it in

1	import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
2	import type { ShopperBasketsV2Types } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
3	import { useShopperBasketsV2Mutation as useShopperBasketsMutation } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
4	import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';
5	
6	/**
7	 * The minimal basket shape this hook needs, regardless of which caller supplies it: the
8	 * post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, wired in this step) passes the resolved value
9	 * of its own `mergeBasket` mutation directly; the cart drawer's render guard
10	 * (`overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, step 4.6 — not yet built) will pass its
11	 * own `useCurrentBasket()` data. `Pick`-narrowed, matching `cartItemMapper.ts`'s own established
12	 * pattern for taking an untyped-at-the-edges SDK response and narrowing it to only the fields a
13	 * pure function actually reads, rather than depending on the exact generic SDK response type
14	 * either caller's own mutation/query hook happens to produce.
15	 */
16	export type CartCapBasket = Pick<ShopperBasketsV2Types.Basket, 'basketId' | 'lastModified' | 'productItems'>;
17	
18	/**
19	 * Outcome of one `capBasketQuantities` call. A discriminated union (typescript.md's guidance for
20	 * variant/state modelling) rather than a boolean-plus-optional-error: each branch is something a
21	 * caller could reasonably want to react to differently, and no AC or copy exists yet for any of
22	 * them (that is `useCartMessages`, step 4.3, not built) — this file only reports what happened,
23	 * it does not decide what the shopper sees.
24	 */
25	export type CartCapResult =
26	  | { status: 'not-needed' }
27	  | { status: 'skipped'; reason: 'mutation-in-flight' | 'already-attempted-this-version' }
28	  | { status: 'corrected' }
29	  | { status: 'error'; error: unknown };
30	
31	/**
32	 * `getMaxOrderQuantity` is typed for a SCAPI product response (`id: string` required — see
33	 * `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`). A basket line item has no `id` field at all: only
34	 * `itemId`/`productId` (confirmed against the generated `BasketProductItem` type — verified via
35	 * a throwaway `tsc` repro that assigning a same-shaped object to a type requiring `id` fails
36	 * with "Property 'id' is missing"), so passing one directly does not type-check, despite it
37	 * carrying the same `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all a real `c_maxOrderQuantity` value would
38	 * arrive through once SFCC-268 ships. `product-item/index.tsx` already lives with the identical
39	 * gap at its own `getMaxOrderQuantity(product)` call site (`type SfccProduct = any`, lines 171
40	 * and 331) — narrowed here with an explicit, commented cast instead of a bare `any` parameter,
41	 * per typescript.md's "no `any` without an inline comment" rule.
42	 */
43	const getLineMaxOrderQuantity = (item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem): number =>
44	  getMaxOrderQuantity(item as unknown as Parameters<typeof getMaxOrderQuantity>[0]);
45	
46	/**
47	 * A line needs correction once its quantity exceeds the cap — i.e. once it reaches the smallest
48	 * over-cap value (`max + 1`; `4` when `max` is `3`) or anything above it. Written as `quantity >
49	 * max` rather than comparing against a separately-named `max + 1` boundary, but the two are the
50	 * same comparison: this must be a "the whole range above the boundary" check, not an
51	 * exact-equality check against a single value — an equality check against `max + 1` alone would
52	 * correctly catch a line at 4 but wrongly leave a line at 5 or more uncorrected, which is
53	 * observably wrong against this hook's own test fixture (a line at 5 must reduce to 3, not stay
54	 * at 5).
55	 */
56	const needsQuantityCorrection = (
57	  item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem,
58	): item is ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem & { quantity: number } =>
59	  typeof item.quantity === 'number' && item.quantity > getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item);
60	
61	/**
62	 * SFCC baskets carry no explicit version counter. `basketId` + `lastModified` change together on
63	 * every write SFCC accepts (both real fields on the generated `Basket` type), so the pair is a
64	 * workable proxy for "the exact basket state a correction was last attempted against" — this is
65	 * this file's own reasoned choice, not sourced from an existing codebase precedent or doc.
66	 */
67	const getBasketVersionKey = (basket: CartCapBasket): string => `${basket.basketId ?? ''}:${basket.lastModified ?? ''}`;
68	
69	/**
70	 * Storage key for "which basket version has a correction already been attempted against."
71	 * Deliberately not a `useRef` — the post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`) and the
72	 * future render guard (step 4.6) each get their own separate `useCartMergeAndCap()` call, and
73	 * therefore their own separate refs, since they mount in two different React component trees. A
74	 * plain ref cannot coordinate between them. Piggybacking on the already-global `QueryClient` (the
75	 * same one `capBasketQuantities`'s own mutation-in-flight guard reads from — see that function's
76	 * own comment) via `getQueryData`/`setQueryData` gives real cross-instance-shared storage without
77	 * inventing a new module-level singleton or Context provider. It is also, unlike a React-render-
78	 * time hook value, live/imperative — reading and then
79	 * immediately writing it inside `capBasketQuantities` with no `await` in between (see that
80	 * function) leaves no window for two near-simultaneous calls to both pass the check before either
81	 * has recorded its attempt, since JavaScript runs that synchronous read-then-write as one
82	 * uninterruptible step.
83	 */
84	const CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY = ['zimmCartMergeAndCap', 'attemptedBasketVersion'] as const;
85	
86	export type UseCartMergeAndCapReturn = {
87	  /**
88	   * Checks every basket line against `getMaxOrderQuantity` and, if any line exceeds its cap,
89	   * issues one `updateItemsInBasket` write reducing every over-cap line to its own max in a
90	   * single request (matching the SFCC-11 plan's "one write" framing even when more than one line
91	   * needs correcting). Resolves only once that write — if one was issued — has fully settled, so
92	   * a caller sequencing merge -> cap -> a future wishlist-resume can `await` this in turn without
93	   * racing it.
94	   */
95	  capBasketQuantities: (basket: CartCapBasket) => Promise<CartCapResult>;
96	};
97	
98	/**
99	 * Hook — the shared "cap" half of SFCC-250's merge-then-cap flow. Two callers share this one
100	 * implementation, not two copies: the post-auth callback inside `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own
101	 * `isRegistered` effect (wired in this step, right after that effect's existing `mergeBasket`
102	 * call), and the cart drawer's render guard, which will live in
103	 * `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (not yet built — a later step, 4.6, wires
104	 * that second call site; this hook is written to support it, not to assume it already exists).
105	 *
106	 * Per rules-of-hooks, call this at the top level of whichever hook or component needs it — never
107	 * from inside a `useEffect` callback — and invoke the returned `capBasketQuantities` function
108	 * itself from inside the effect/render path instead.
109	 *
110	 * @returns `capBasketQuantities`, the one function both callers invoke.
111	 */
112	export const useCartMergeAndCap = (): UseCartMergeAndCapReturn => {
113	  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
114	  const updateItemsInBasket = useShopperBasketsMutation('updateItemsInBasket');
115	
116	  const capBasketQuantities = async (basket: CartCapBasket): Promise<CartCapResult> => {
117	    // No-op while any mutation is in flight (this hook's own prior correction, the merge that
118	    // just ran, a shopper's manual quantity edit — anything) so this can never race a write
119	    // already under way. See this function's own JSDoc.
120	    //
121	    // REWORK (round 1, Tester-confirmed defect): this must be a LIVE read taken at the moment
122	    // this function actually runs — not a React-render-time value closed over at this hook's own
123	    // top level. `capBasketQuantities` is captured once by its caller and invoked later, from
124	    // inside an async callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s `mergeBasket.mutate(...).onSuccess`,
125	    // itself only reachable after a real network round trip) with no guarantee that hook instance
126	    // re-renders in between. A `useIsMutating()` value read at this hook's own top level (the
127	    // original approach here) would still reflect whatever mutation count existed at that earlier
128	    // render, not the real state at the moment this guard actually needs to check it.
129	    //
130	    // `queryClient.isMutating(filters?)` (confirmed against the installed
131	    // `@tanstack/query-core@4.43.0` source — a single deduped version across this project's whole
132	    // dependency tree, per `npm ls @tanstack/react-query` — `node_modules/@tanstack/query-core/
133	    // build/lib/queryClient.esm.js`: `isMutating(filters) { return this.mutationCache.findAll(
134	    // {...filters, fetching: true}).length; }`) computes this fresh from the live mutation cache
135	    // on every call. It is the exact same computation `useIsMutating()` itself wraps in
136	    // `useSyncExternalStore` for React reactivity (`node_modules/@tanstack/react-query/build/lib/
137	    // useIsMutating.esm.js`: `() => queryClient.isMutating(filters)`), just read directly instead
138	    // of through a render-synced subscription — so this preserves the exact same "every mutation
139	    // anywhere in the app" scope this guard has always had (commerce-sdk-react's basket mutation
140	    // hooks set no `mutationKey`, so an unscoped call is still the only reading that sees all of
141	    // them), it now just reads that scope live instead of stale.
142	    if (queryClient.isMutating() > 0) {
143	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'mutation-in-flight' };
144	    }
145	
146	    const correctedItems = (basket.productItems ?? []).filter(needsQuantityCorrection).map((item) => ({
147	      itemId: item.itemId,
148	      productId: item.productId,
149	      quantity: getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item),
150	    }));
151	
152	    if (correctedItems.length === 0) {
153	      return { status: 'not-needed' };
154	    }
155	
156	    if (!basket.basketId) {
157	      // No basketId means there is nothing valid to address a write at — surface this as an
158	      // error rather than silently doing nothing, so a caller can tell "nothing needed fixing"
159	      // apart from "something needed fixing and couldn't be".
160	      return { status: 'error', error: new Error('useCartMergeAndCap: basket is missing a basketId.') };
161	    }
162	
163	    const versionKey = getBasketVersionKey(basket);
164	    if (queryClient.getQueryData<string>(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY) === versionKey) {
165	      // Loop guard: a correction has already been attempted against this exact basket state,
166	      // whether it succeeded or failed — do not retry it. See CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY's own
167	      // comment for why this is a live cache read rather than a per-instance ref, and why
168	      // setting it below, before the `await`, is what keeps this race-free.
169	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'already-attempted-this-version' };
170	    }
171	    queryClient.setQueryData(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY, versionKey);
172	
173	    try {
174	      await updateItemsInBasket.mutateAsync({
175	        parameters: { basketId: basket.basketId },
176	        body: correctedItems,
177	      });
178	      return { status: 'corrected' };
179	    } catch (error) {
180	      // Surfaced to the caller, not retried: the version is already marked attempted above, so a
181	      // later call against this same unchanged basket state returns 'skipped' rather than
182	      // hammering the server again — no retry storm.
183	      return { status: 'error', error };
184	    }
185	  };
186	
187	  return { capBasketQuantities };
188	};

1	import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
2	
3	/**
4	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no TypeScript types (AGENTS.md's "Commerce SDK types not
5	 * importable" gotcha) — `use-toast.js` falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s catch-all
6	 * `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'` (a shorthand ambient module declaration that
7	 * types the whole module `any` — see that file's own comment, and
8	 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s identical narrow-local-type pattern for
9	 * another untyped base function), so the real `useToast()` return value is implicitly `any`.
10	 * Declared narrow here, covering only the two fields this file actually sends (`title`, `status`)
11	 * rather than the base hook's full options surface (`description`, `action`, `position`,
12	 * `duration`, `variant`, `isClosable`) — nothing in this file uses those, so typing them would be
13	 * speculative. `status`'s four values are copied verbatim from the base hook's real accepted set
14	 * (not narrowed to only `'success' | 'warning'`), so a later message that genuinely needs `'error'`
15	 * or `'info'` — SFCC-404's rework, or any message added after this step — is already covered
16	 * without a signature change here.
17	 *
18	 * This is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee — TypeScript
19	 * allows asserting `any` to any narrower type with no check. The real proof is this file's own
20	 * test, which asserts the exact object the mocked toast function is called with.
21	 */
22	type CartToastStatus = 'success' | 'error' | 'info' | 'warning';
23	type CartToastFn = (options: { title: string; status: CartToastStatus }) => void;
24	
25	/**
26	 * The three real cart messages this step ships, copy verbatim from Figma (SFCC-11 plan step 4.3)
27	 * — this file never derives or paraphrases copy, only interpolates a product name into the one
28	 * message that needs it. SFCC-272's own AC text describes a generic stacked wording ("Item added
29	 * to Wishlist") for when more than one item has been added — deliberately not built here: a toast
30	 * has no aggregation concept, so that copy is only reachable once SFCC-404 ships real message
31	 * stacking. Until then every add uses this product-named variant, one toast per add.
32	 */
33	const getAddedToWishlistMessage = (productName: string): string => `${productName} added to Wishlist`;
34	const ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST_MESSAGE = 'An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist';
35	const MAX_QUANTITY_REACHED_MESSAGE = 'An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity';
36	
37	export type UseCartMessagesReturn = {
38	  /**
39	   * SFCC-272 AC5 — a single product was moved from the cart to the wishlist. `productName` is
40	   * interpolated into the copy on every call — never hardcode a specific product's name at a call
41	   * site. `success` status.
42	   */
43	  notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => void;
44	  /**
45	   * SFCC-272 AC6 — the item already exists in the shopper's wishlist; the caller leaves the cart
46	   * line untouched. Verbatim copy, no interpolation. `warning` status — see
47	   * `notifyMaxQuantityReached`'s own doc for why cart feedback that doesn't block anything reads
48	   * as a warning in this build, not an error.
49	   */
50	  notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => void;
51	  /**
52	   * CAI-017 / SFCC-250 — a cart line has reached its maximum orderable quantity (the line is
53	   * already capped by `useCartMergeAndCap` before this ever fires). `warning`, not `error`:
54	   * CAI-017's own requirement text says "an error message will be displayed", but the Figma
55	   * rendering uses the warning variant and SFCC-250 AC4 confirms this never blocks checkout — this
56	   * build's own gate resolved the wording as meaning user-facing feedback, not literally Chakra's
57	   * error severity (the same reconciliation `ZimmInlineMessage`'s own `variant` prop documents —
58	   * `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx`: "a caller may
59	   * legitimately pass `variant=\"warning\"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word
60	   * `error`").
61	   */
62	  notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => void;
63	};
64	
65	/**
66	 * Hook — the one surface every cart toast message (success and warning today; whatever SFCC-404's
67	 * real stacking/aggregation rework needs later, including a genuine error) is sent through.
68	 * `emitCartMessage` below is the single call to the underlying toast function — a future rework
69	 * swaps what happens inside this one file, not a hunt across the cart UI for every place that
70	 * fires a toast.
71	 *
72	 * Wraps the **base** `useToast` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast`) rather than a
73	 * new `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` — that path does not exist, and creating it would be an
74	 * unbudgeted Tier 2 change (`protectedFiles.md` would route it to both squads plus tier-2/tier-1
75	 * approvers). See the SFCC-11 plan's own resolved open question 4. This hook is the real "one
76	 * handler" the plan asks for; the base hook underneath it is just the interim renderer SFCC-404
77	 * replaces.
78	 *
79	 * @returns the three named cart-message senders callers actually invoke today. `emitCartMessage`
80	 * itself is intentionally not returned — nothing outside this file needs to send an
81	 * uncatalogued/arbitrary message yet, and a future message is one new named function here, not a
82	 * reason to widen this hook's public surface.
83	 */
84	export const useCartMessages = (): UseCartMessagesReturn => {
85	  // Real return type is implicit `any` (see CartToastFn's own docblock above) — asserted to the
86	  // local narrow type rather than left as `any`, so every call below is checked against the shape
87	  // this file actually depends on.
88	  const toast = useToast() as CartToastFn;
89	
90	  const emitCartMessage = (title: string, status: CartToastStatus): void => {
91	    // SFCC-404: this is the one real call to the underlying toast function. When SFCC-404's real
92	    // stacking/aggregation rework lands, this is the only line that changes.
93	    toast({ title, status });
94	  };
95	
96	  return {
97	    notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => emitCartMessage(getAddedToWishlistMessage(productName), 'success'),
98	    notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => emitCartMessage(ALREADY_IN_WISHLIST_MESSAGE, 'warning'),
99	    notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => emitCartMessage(MAX_QUANTITY_REACHED_MESSAGE, 'warning'),
100	  };
101	};
102

import type { SystemStyleObject } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED } from 'app/components/ui-kits/zimmCartItemShared';

/** State the component feeds in so the recipe can resolve the value display's dimmed state.
 *  Named `disabled` (not e.g. `isUnavailable`) to match the resolution-prop convention already
 *  used by every other function-form baseStyle in this codebase (zimmTextInput.css.ts's own
 *  `disabled` key) — `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s PROP_COMBINATIONS harness only
 *  exercises the fixed key set `{inverse, disabled, hasError, focused, filled}`, so a
 *  differently-named boolean here would never have its `true` branch walked by that guard. */
export type ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps = {
  disabled?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Recipe — cart-line quantity stepper (SFCC-271). Two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls sit
 * either side of a numeric value display; all hover/press/focus/disabled states for the buttons
 * themselves live entirely in zimmButton.css.ts (untouched by this file — see index.tsx, which
 * composes ZimmButton rather than restyling it).
 *
 * `root` — the flex row. Gap is 8px (`var(--zimm-scale-xs)` — foundation/spacing.ts's `xs` is
 * `0.5rem`/8px exactly, so this needs no new token). Deliberate, disclosed departure from
 * Figma's own raw annotation, which shows a 12px gap around a bare 12px glyph with no drawn
 * touch target at all. ZimmButton's `icon` size variant already resolves both buttons to a 24px
 * touch target (zimmButton.css.ts `sizes.icon` — `minW`/`minH`: `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, cited
 * there against WCAG 2.2 AA SC 2.5.8, and matching the Figma node's own literal name
 * `touchTarget` at value 24) — i.e. 6px of invisible padding is already added on every side of
 * each 12px glyph before this gap is even applied. An 8px authored gap between the two 24px
 * button boxes therefore reproduces the ~12px glyph-to-glyph spacing Figma's raw annotation
 * intended (6px inset + 8px gap + 6px inset from centre-of-glyph to centre-of-glyph ≈ the
 * annotated 12px), without shrinking either button below its accessible 24px target — the
 * alternative (an 8px gap measured glyph-edge to glyph-edge with no inset accounted for) would
 * under-space them relative to Figma; this recipe's 8px is the touch-target-aware equivalent,
 * not a straight copy of the raw annotation.
 *
 * `value` — the numeric display. No Figma node or type-style was supplied for this specific text
 * in this build step; `body2Strong` (14px / 500 weight / 18px line-height, typography.ts) is the
 * nearest existing textStyle — PROVISIONAL pending UI-designer confirmation, same disclosure
 * pattern as zimmSizeSelector.css.ts's own oneSize label. Dims to OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED when
 * `disabled` (the whole control is OOS/unavailable, not just one bound) — sourced from
 * zimmCartItemShared.ts rather than restated here or imported from zimmButton.css.ts, so the
 * value display and the two buttons beside it (which get their own dimming entirely from
 * zimmButton.css.ts's `icon` variant, once the caller passes `ariaDisabled` through — nothing
 * about that is duplicated here) can never visually drift apart, without this recipe reaching
 * into an unrelated atom's styling module for the number. Applying the SAME opacity to `root`
 * as well would double it up on the buttons (0.4 × 0.4 = 0.16, not 0.4) — deliberately scoped to
 * `value` only for that reason.
 */
export const ZimmQuantityStepper = {
  parts: ['root', 'value'],
  baseStyle: ({ disabled }: ZimmQuantityStepperStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    root: {
      display: 'inline-flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
    },
    value: {
      display: 'inline-flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      justifyContent: 'center',
      textStyle: 'body2Strong',
      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
      opacity: disabled ? OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED : 1,
    },
  }),
};

1	/**
2	 * Shared constants for the SFCC-11 cart build. Same role as theme/components/footerShared.ts /
3	 * headerShared.ts — see .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Cross-file shared values" section:
4	 * a value needed by more than one file goes here once, imported everywhere it's needed, so two
5	 * call sites can't independently retype the same number and silently drift apart. Placed
6	 * alongside `ui-kits/` (rather than `theme/components/`, where footerShared.ts/headerShared.ts
7	 * live) because this cart build's first consumer is a component-local recipe co-located under
8	 * `ui-kits/molecules/`, not a `theme/components/`-resident recipe — later commits in this same
9	 * build may add more cart-item constants here, but that is not yet built and is not asserted as
10	 * done by this comment.
11	 */
12	
13	// Icon-button disabled opacity for the cart quantity stepper (ZimmQuantityStepper, SFCC-271).
14	// Intentionally the SAME numeric value as zimmButton.css.ts's own OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED (0.4,
15	// see that file's `icon`/`iconInverse` variants) — not imported from there, because that file is
16	// a Tier 2 recipe this build step does not touch, and a constant needed by a sibling recipe
17	// (zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts) plus this component's own tests should not have to reach into an
18	// unrelated atom's styling module for an unrelated number. Kept here as its own named constant,
19	// deliberately equal, so both places that dim something to "the disabled look" (ZimmButton's own
20	// icon variant, applied automatically once ariaDisabled is passed, and this stepper's own value
21	// display, which is not a ZimmButton and so has no such variant of its own) render at the
22	// identical opacity instead of two independently-authored numbers that only start out matching.
23	// Per conventions.md > "No magic numbers or strings" — a named constant, not an inline literal.
24	export const OPACITY_ICON_DISABLED = 0.4;

<Stack layerStyle="cardBordered" align="flex-start" {...containerStyles}>
          <Flex sx={styles.row} width="full" backgroundColor="white">
            <CartItemVariantImage />
            <Stack sx={styles.details} flex={1}>
              <Flex sx={styles.info}>
                <Box sx={styles.itemInfoContainer}>
                  <Flex sx={styles.itemInfo}>
                    <CartItemVariantName />
                    <CartItemVariantPrice align="left" currency={activeCurrency} />
                  </Flex>
                  <CartItemVariantAttributes excludeBonusLabel combineAttributeValues />
                </Box>
                {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                  <HideOnMobile>{deliveryActions}</HideOnMobile>
                )}
              </Flex>

              {!hideStepperAndActions && deliveryActions && !product.bonusProductLineItem && (
                <HideOnDesktop>{deliveryActions}</HideOnDesktop>
              )}

              <Flex align="flex-end" justify="space-between">
                <Stack spacing={1}>
                  {!hideStepperAndActions &&
                    !(isRemoving && product.bonusProductLineItem) &&
                    (product.bonusProductLineItem ? (
                      <BonusProductQuantity product={product} />
                    ) : (
                      <ZimmQuantityStepper
                        quantity={quantity}
                        min={1}
                        max={getMaxOrderQuantity(product)}
                        onDecrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
                        onIncrement={handleStepperQuantityChange}
                        ariaDescribedBy={message ? messageId : undefined}
                      />
                    ))}
                </Stack>
                <Stack>{!hideStepperAndActions && <HideOnMobile>{primaryAction}</HideOnMobile>}</Stack>
              </Flex>

              {/* SFCC-795 (plan step 3.3): discount label, directly beneath the stepper/price row
                  above, ahead of the inline message below — prop-driven only, no empty node when
                  omitted. See the `discountLabel` prop's own JSDoc for the styling citation. */}
              {discountLabel && (
                <ZimmInlineMessage variant="success" text={discountLabel} dataTestId="zimm-discount-label" />
              )}

              {/* SFCC-795 §11.2: sits between the stepper (above) and the actions row (the
                  existing inventory Box below, secondaryActions, and the mobile primaryAction
                  block further down) — prop-driven only, see this file's own docblock.
                  `id={messageId}` (SFCC-795 plan step 3.6) is the other half of the stepper's
                  `ariaDescribedBy` above — same id, both sides only present together. */}
              {message && <ZimmInlineMessage variant={message.variant} text={message.text} id={messageId} />}

              <Box>
                {product && showInventoryMessage && (
                  <Fade in={true}>
                    <Text color="orange.600" fontWeight={600}>
                      {inventoryMessage}
                    </Text>
                  </Fade>
                )}
              </Box>

              {!hideStepperAndActions && secondaryActions}
            </Stack>
          </Flex>

          {!hideStepperAndActions && (
            <HideOnDesktop>
              <Box w={'full'}>{primaryAction}</Box>
            </HideOnDesktop>
          )}
        </Stack>
      </ItemVariantProvider>
    </Box>
  );
};

export default ProductItem;

2	import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
3	import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';

5	const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';
6	
7	export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
8	  /**
9	   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
10	   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
11	   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
12	   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
13	   *
14	   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
15	   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
16	   */
17	  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
18	  /**
19	   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
20	   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
21	   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
22	   * §11.2 exact copy).
23	   */
24	  text: string;
25	  /**
26	   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
27	   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
28	   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
29	   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
30	   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
31	   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
32	   */
33	  dataTestId?: string;
34	  /**
35	   * SFCC-795 plan step 3.6 (accessibility sweep): stable id for a caller to reference via
36	   * `aria-describedby` on the control this message is actually about — the same
37	   * id-on-the-message + `aria-describedby`-on-the-control pairing `zimmTextInput/index.tsx`
38	   * already uses for its own helper/error text (`helperId`/`errorId`). Undefined (every existing
39	   * caller today) omits the `id` attribute entirely, unchanged from before this prop existed.
40	   *
41	   * Consumed by `product-item/index.tsx`: this message's one real-world consumer is
42	   * `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls, so the id is forwarded as
43	   * `aria-describedby` on both of those buttons, not on a wrapping element — ARIA description is
44	   * computed per focused node, not inherited from an ancestor, so a screen-reader user tabbing to
45	   * either button would not hear a description set only on a container (confirmed against
46	   * `zimmDropdown/index.tsx`'s own precedent, which sets `aria-describedby` directly on its native
47	   * `chakra.button` trigger for the same reason). Getting `aria-describedby` onto the icon variant
48	   * at all required a small, additive addition to `ZimmButton` itself (`ariaDescribedBy` on
49	   * `ZimmIconButtonProps`, `zimmButton/index.tsx`) — `ZimmLabelButtonProps` already had the
50	   * equivalent prop, `ZimmIconButtonProps` did not.
51	   */
52	  id?: string;
53	};
54	
55	/**
56	 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
57	 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
58	 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
59	 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
60	 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
61	 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
62	 *
63	 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
64	 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
65	 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
66	 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
67	 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
68	 *
69	 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
70	 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
71	 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
72	 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
73	 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
74	 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
75	 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
76	 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
77	 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
78	 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
79	 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.

81	 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,

86	 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
87	 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
88	 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with

import React from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmIcon } from 'app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon';

const ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE = 'ZimmInlineMessage';

export type ZimmInlineMessageProps = {
  /**
   * Colour/severity only — this atom never decides which one applies. A caller may legitimately
   * pass `variant="warning"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word "error" (the cart
   * max-quantity message is exactly this case) — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for
   * why that's a deliberate word-vs-severity reconciliation, not a mismatch to fix here.
   *
   * `success` added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull, 2026-09-18) for
   * the cart-line discount label ("20% off applied") — see this component's own docblock below.
   */
  variant: 'error' | 'warning' | 'success';
  /**
   * Message copy, rendered verbatim. This atom never derives, hardcodes, or paraphrases copy — a
   * caller supplies the already-resolved string (e.g. "This item is unavailable", "Quantity
   * unavailable in this size", "Maximum purchase quantity reached for this size" — SFCC-795
   * §11.2 exact copy).
   */
  text: string;
  /**
   * Overrides the root element's `data-testid`, defaulting to the pre-existing hardcoded
   * `'zimm-inline-message'` — every caller that omits this keeps that exact default, unchanged.
   * Added SFCC-795 plan step 3.3: a single cart line can now render both a discount label
   * (`variant="success"`) and an error/warning `message` at once (product-item/index.tsx), so two
   * `ZimmInlineMessage` instances can appear on one line — without a distinct testid per instance,
   * `getByTestId('zimm-inline-message')` would match both and throw.
   */
  dataTestId?: string;
  /**
   * SFCC-795 plan step 3.6 (accessibility sweep): stable id for a caller to reference via
   * `aria-describedby` on the control this message is actually about — the same
   * id-on-the-message + `aria-describedby`-on-the-control pairing `zimmTextInput/index.tsx`
   * already uses for its own helper/error text (`helperId`/`errorId`). Undefined (every existing
   * caller today) omits the `id` attribute entirely, unchanged from before this prop existed.
   *
   * Consumed by `product-item/index.tsx`: this message's one real-world consumer is
   * `ZimmQuantityStepper`'s two `ZimmButton variant="icon"` controls, so the id is forwarded as
   * `aria-describedby` on both of those buttons, not on a wrapping element — ARIA description is
   * computed per focused node, not inherited from an ancestor, so a screen-reader user tabbing to
   * either button would not hear a description set only on a container (confirmed against
   * `zimmDropdown/index.tsx`'s own precedent, which sets `aria-describedby` directly on its native
   * `chakra.button` trigger for the same reason). Getting `aria-describedby` onto the icon variant
   * at all required a small, additive addition to `ZimmButton` itself (`ariaDescribedBy` on
   * `ZimmIconButtonProps`, `zimmButton/index.tsx`) — `ZimmLabelButtonProps` already had the
   * equivalent prop, `ZimmIconButtonProps` did not.
   */
  id?: string;
};

/**
 * Atom — cart-line inline status message (SFCC-795 §11.2, plan step 3.2). Presentation only:
 * renders whatever `variant`/`text` it is given and never determines availability itself.
 * OOS/partial-OOS detection is SFCC-282's, "Unavailable" detection is SFCC-796's — both
 * later-sprint tickets this component does not, and should not, anticipate. No low-stock variant
 * exists in `ZimmInlineMessageProps['variant']` — a separate requirement explicitly forbids
 * low-stock messaging at the cart level (see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts).
 *
 * `aria-live="polite"` matches the same treatment this codebase already gives another transient,
 * non-input cart-line status value — ZimmQuantityStepper's own quantity display (its `value`
 * part, zimmQuantityStepper/index.tsx) carries the identical `aria-live="polite"` treatment — so
 * a shopper using assistive tech is told about a message that appears/changes after their own
 * action, without requiring focus to move to it.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework (Marcel's own visual checkpoint against the real Figma file): the `warning`
 * variant renders a leading `info-solid` icon, `error` never does — confirmed against 3 real
 * cart-item instances in Figma file QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs: the two error-copy states (FULLY OOS
 * node 9323-101979, PARTIAL OOS node 9323-98397) have no icon in their message sub-tree; the
 * warning-copy state's own "Cart Item" instance (9323:106685 — one of 5 per-item rows inside the
 * "WARNINGS SHOWN" frame's "Cart-item-group", not that frame's separate SFCC-404
 * "Cart-level-messages" sibling — see zimmInlineMessage.css.ts for the full parent-chain
 * citation) does. The icon is `aria-hidden` — the
 * message's own text plus `aria-live` already carry the full meaning to assistive tech, so the
 * icon is a purely visual (sighted-only) reinforcement of a severity already conveyed by colour
 * and copy, not an independent piece of information.
 *
 * SFCC-795 rework, part 2 (Marcel's direct Figma inspector pull for the discount-label node,
 * 2026-09-18): a third variant, `success`, renders the cart-line discount label ("20% off
 * applied", product-item/index.tsx's `discountLabel` prop). That element used to be a bespoke
 * `<Text>` styled to match the WRONG Figma node (item-variant.css.ts's `colourSize` part, a
 * different, medium-weight node); the real pulled node is `color:
 * var(--alias-color-text-success, #2D5A3D); font-size: var(--brand-font-size-300, 12px);
 * font-weight: 400; line-height: var(--brand-font-lineHeight-450, 18px)` — "Default/Caption", the
 * exact same regular-weight 12px/18px node family `error`/`warning` already render, coloured with
 * this codebase's own `status.success` token (byte-identical to the pulled hex — see
 * zimmInlineMessage.css.ts's own docblock for the token chain). Confirmed directly with Marcel:
 * `success` carries no icon, same as `error` — the icon condition below is unchanged and
 * `'success'` correctly falls through it.
 *
 * @param props see ZimmInlineMessageProps
 */
export const ZimmInlineMessage = ({
  variant,
  text,
  dataTestId = 'zimm-inline-message',
  id,
}: ZimmInlineMessageProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_INLINE_MESSAGE_RECIPE, { variant });

  return (
    <chakra.div id={id} __css={styles.root} aria-live="polite" data-testid={dataTestId}>
      {variant === 'warning' && <ZimmIcon type="info-solid" size="md" aria-hidden />}
      <chakra.p __css={styles.text}>{text}</chakra.p>
    </chakra.div>
  );
};

1	import type { ShopperBasketsTypes, ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
2	import { findImageGroupBy } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/image-groups-utils';
3	import { getDisplayVariationValues } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
4	
5	/*
6	 * Converts an SDK basket `productItem` into a self-contained display-data shape, mirroring the
7	 * `productListCardMapper.ts` precedent (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`,
8	 * PR #85) for how a page-scoped SDK-to-props mapper is organised in this codebase: exported
9	 * "select"-prefixed functions (that file exports three: `selectGalleryImages`,
10	 * `selectSizeChipValues`, `selectProductListCard` - corrected here, an earlier draft of this
11	 * comment said "a single" one, which was wrong), an untyped-base-package input narrowed to a
12	 * local type, and a `.test.ts` asserting the mapped shape directly (see that file's own
13	 * `ProductListSearchHit`/`RawImage` pattern, mirrored below for `CartLineItem`/`CartItemImage`).
14	 *
15	 * Disclosed design choice, not a directly sourced requirement (flagged per this step's own
16	 * instructions): `ProductItem`/`ItemVariantProvider` (`overrides/app/components/product-item/
17	 * index.tsx:140`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/index.tsx:43`) both currently declare
18	 * their real data-carrying prop as the raw untyped basket/product object itself
19	 * (`product`/`variant`, both `SfccProduct`/`SfccVariant = any`) — today's leaves read every
20	 * display field (image, name, combined attributes) directly off that object via
21	 * `useItemVariant()`, not from individually-mapped props. This mapper is, per this step's plan
22	 * text, "an as-yet-unused-by-anything-else container-layer function" — it does not change or
23	 * feed either of those two files (out of this step's scope). What it produces instead is a pure,
24	 * tested equivalent of the specific per-field computations those leaves and
25	 * `product-quantity-picker.tsx`/`use-derived-product.js` already perform internally off that same
26	 * raw object (image+alt, combined colour/size, quantity, stepQuantity) — ready for whichever
27	 * future step decides how a real page hands data down, without having modified any of those
28	 * existing files.
29	 *
30	 * `CartLineItem` models the REAL runtime shape a basket line item has by the time it reaches
31	 * those leaves: the un-overridden base cart page never passes the raw `basket.productItems[i]`
32	 * alone — it merges it with the matching full `Product` (fetched separately via `useProducts`)
33	 * before handing it down: `product={{...productItem, ...productsByItemId[productItem.itemId],
34	 * price: productItem.price, quantity: ...}}` (see
35	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item-list/index.jsx`, the
36	 * `<ProductItem product={...}>` call). `imageGroups`/`variationAttributes`/`variationValues`/
37	 * `stepQuantity`/`name` all come from that merged-in `Product` half, not from
38	 * `ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem` itself (confirmed against its generated fields — it has no
39	 * image/variation/stepQuantity fields at all beyond its own `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all).
40	 *
41	 * Both halves are `Pick`'d, not intersected raw (zm-tester, SFCC-11 step 3.4 finding): the real
42	 * generated `ProductItem` type carries the identical `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all the comment
43	 * above already calls out on `Product`. Intersecting it raw would silently resolve a typo'd field
44	 * name (or a nonexistent one) to `any` instead of a compile error — empirically confirmed harmless
45	 * today (every real access below is spelled correctly) but a real, latent gap a future edit could
46	 * hit silently. `Pick`ing both halves closes it the same way on both sides.
47	 */
48	type CartLineItem = Pick<ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem, 'itemId' | 'productId' | 'quantity' | 'productName'> &
49	  Pick<
50	    ShopperProductsTypes.Product,
51	    'imageGroups' | 'variationAttributes' | 'variationValues' | 'stepQuantity' | 'name'
52	  >;
53	
54	type CartItemImage = {
55	  src?: string;
56	  /**
57	   * Always a string, never undefined — even when there's no image at all (falls back to the
58	   * item's own name, then `''`). See `selectCartItemImage`'s own doc comment for the fallback
59	   * chain and why this differs from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `toCardImage`, which returns
60	   * `undefined` for the whole image on a miss instead.
61	   */
62	  alt: string;
63	};
64	
65	type CartItemMapperResult = {
66	  itemId?: string;
67	  productId?: string;
68	  name: string;
69	  image: CartItemImage;
70	  combinedAttributes: string;
71	  quantity?: number;
72	  stepQuantity: number;
73	};
74	
75	/**
76	 * Matches `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product.js:38`'s own
77	 * `product?.stepQuantity || 1` exactly — reused as a value, not a shared import, since that hook
78	 * itself isn't a pure function this module can call (it's stateful, `useState`-backed).
79	 */
80	const DEFAULT_STEP_QUANTITY = 1;
81	
82	/**
83	 * Selects this line item's display image, always returning a defined `alt` even when there is no
84	 * image at all (unlike `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `toCardImage`, which returns `undefined` for
85	 * the whole image on a miss — a PLP card can legitimately skip rendering entirely when it has
86	 * nothing to show; a cart line item cannot, per this step's own pass criteria).
87	 *
88	 * The lookup itself reuses `findImageGroupBy` exactly as
89	 * `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-image.tsx:70-73` already does (same `viewType:
90	 * 'small'` / `selectedVariationAttributes` call) rather than reimplementing image-group matching.
91	 */
92	const selectCartItemImage = (item: CartLineItem): CartItemImage => {
93	  const image = findImageGroupBy(item.imageGroups, {
94	    viewType: 'small',
95	    selectedVariationAttributes: item.variationValues,
96	  })?.images?.[0];
97	
98	  return {
99	    src: image?.disBaseLink || image?.link,
100	    alt: image?.alt || item.productName || item.name || '',
101	  };
102	};
103	
104	/**
105	 * Combines the colour and size variation values into the single string the Figma cart-item spec
106	 * calls for, reusing the exact mechanism
107	 * `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes.tsx:98,148-150` already uses for its own
108	 * `combineAttributeValues` behaviour (`getDisplayVariationValues(...)` then
109	 * `Object.values(...).join(', ')`) rather than reimplementing string-combining from scratch.
110	 *
111	 * Ordering is inherited from that same call, not independently re-sorted here: it reflects
112	 * whichever order the incoming `variationValues` object's own keys are in (see
113	 * `getDisplayVariationValues`'s `Object.entries(values).reduce(...)`,
114	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:30`). This is the
115	 * identical mechanism `item-attributes.tsx`'s own docblock (line 31) already cites as producing
116	 * "Lilac Sand, One size" (colour, size) for real Zimmermann catalog data —
117	 * `product-item/index.tsx`'s docblock (line 44) corroborates the same combined-string behaviour
118	 * generically ("colour, size") without repeating that specific example. This function inherits
119	 * that already-verified behaviour rather than re-guaranteeing the order independently.
120	 */
121	const selectCombinedAttributes = (item: CartLineItem): string => {
122	  const variationValues = getDisplayVariationValues(item.variationAttributes, item.variationValues);
123	  return variationValues ? Object.values(variationValues).join(', ') : '';
124	};
125	
126	/**
127	 * Maps one basket line item (already merged with its full product data — see this file's own
128	 * module docblock) to a plain display-data shape: image, name, one combined colour/size string,
129	 * and quantity/stepQuantity passed through. Pure function, no hooks — keeps every consumer in B3
130	 * prop-driven with no data-fetching hook in a leaf, per this step's own plan text.
131	 */
132	export const selectCartItemProps = (item: CartLineItem): CartItemMapperResult => ({
133	  itemId: item.itemId,
134	  productId: item.productId,
135	  name: item.productName || item.name || '',
136	  image: selectCartItemImage(item),
137	  combinedAttributes: selectCombinedAttributes(item),
138	  quantity: item.quantity,
139	  stepQuantity: item.stepQuantity || DEFAULT_STEP_QUANTITY,
140	});

import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe — the "Remove" / "Move to Wishlist" action-links row (SFCC-270 AC8, SFCC-272). Single
 * style, no parts: both links get their full visual treatment from `ZimmLink`'s own recipe
 * (`zimmLink.css.ts`, size `small` — capitalize, 12px/500/14px-lh, plus that recipe's own
 * hover/focus-visible states); this recipe only owns the row's own layout, matching
 * `zimmLink/zimmLink.css.ts`'s own single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` — Figma specifies 25px (§11.10(4) of the SFCC-11 plan); no `--zimm-scale-*` step lands on
 * 25 (foundation/spacing.ts's steps go ...m:16px, l:20px, xl:24px, 2xl:32px... — confirmed no
 * 25px entry), so this snaps to the nearest existing token, 24px (`xl`), and records the raw
 * design value here rather than typing an unregistered one-off literal.
 *
 * `color` on each link is NOT set here: `ZimmLink`'s own `link.default` alias
 * (`foundation/colour.ts:87`, `grey[900]`) and `foundation/colour.ts:61`'s `text.default` (also
 * `grey[900]`) are the same primitive, so plain `<ZimmLink>` already renders the colour this
 * component's own spec calls for — adding a second, competing colour declaration here would be
 * exactly the anti-pattern `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "One canonical styling surface
 * per component type" section warns against (a value that can drift from the atom's own recipe
 * over time instead of there being only one place it's declared).
 */
export const ZimmCartItemActions = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // Figma: 25px, snapped to the nearest token (24px)
  },
});
