input.message:
## Branch check
`feature/SFCC-11_cart` (confirmed via `git branch --show-current`) — not `develop`/`main`, safe to write.

## What I built (commit 16 of 20, step 4.4)
New folder `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmCartItemActions/`:
- `index.tsx` — the `ZimmCartItemActions` molecule (Remove / Move to Wishlist links)
- `zimmCartItemActions.css.ts` — its recipe (single-style, registered as `ZimmCartItemActions`)
- `usePendingWishlistItem.ts` — the authorized co-located hook for pending-item-across-auth
- `index.test.tsx`, `index.stories.tsx`, `usePendingWishlistItem.test.ts`

One line added in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (import + registration). Nothing else touched — confirmed via `git status --porcelain`.

## Two things I would not build as literally instructed — both need your ratification, not mine

**1. "Resume fires after merge and cap" (pass criterion 11) rests on a false premise about `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`.**
Consequence: if step 4.6 wires the real SDK calls the way this step's brief describes, a guest's wishlist-move can fire while the guest→registered basket merge is still in flight — the exact "shopper's items are gone" class of bug step 4.1 exists to prevent, just for the wishlist-move path instead of the basket-count path.
Mechanism: I read `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:173-241` directly. `onAuthSuccess?.()` fires **synchronously, before `mergeBasket.mutate(...)` is even called** — not after merge-and-cap resolve as the brief states ("which per steps 4.1/4.2 already fires after merge-and-cap resolve"). `capBasketQuantities(mergedBasket)` only runs later, inside `mergeBasket`'s own `onSuccess`, fire-and-forget, with nothing chained after it. `useCartMergeAndCap.test.ts`'s "sequencing" test (which the brief cites as proof) only proves `capBasketQuantities` itself resolves after its own write settles, using local test-only stand-ins for merge and resume — it does not prove the real `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` actually chains a resume after cap, because it doesn't.
Fix: I wired my resume trigger to `onAuthSuccess` anyway — it's the only signal this step's files have access to, `usePendingWishlistItem`'s own tests pass criteria 9/10 correctly in isolation, and the actual defect only materializes once step 4.6 wires real SDK calls behind `onMoveToWishlist`. I did not write a comment asserting the false "fires after merge and cap" ordering. **Before step 4.6 starts, someone needs to either move the merge-call's resume signal to fire from inside `capBasketQuantities(mergedBasket)`'s own resolution (a `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` change, out of this step's scope) or accept the race and use `productId`-based re-resolution to make it safe regardless (see next point).**

**2. "`ZimmCartItemActions` calling `useWishlistAuthDrawer` directly is correct" contradicts the plan's own cardinality rule.**
Consequence: built as the brief describes, a cart with N items would mount N `useForm`s, 3N `useAuthHelper`s, N `useAuthModal`s and N drawers — exactly the shape the same plan step explicitly rejects two paragraphs earlier ("one `useWishlistAuthDrawer` instance per line item ... untenable against this project's mobile-page-speed priority").
Mechanism: `ZimmCartItemActions` is necessarily rendered once per cart line (supplied into each `product-item`'s own `secondaryActions` slot). The plan requires exactly ONE `useWishlistAuthDrawer` instance for the whole cart (`intentId: 'cart-wishlist'`, singular). A hook call inside a per-row component cannot be "one instance" — I checked whether a conditionally-rendered wrapper could reconcile this (mount the drawer only after the first click) and it doesn't work: `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` needs to wrap the trigger's `onClick` *before* the click happens to intercept it.
Fix: I built `ZimmCartItemActions` to receive `isGuest: boolean` and `onGuestWishlistClick: () => void` as **props**, not by calling the hook itself. The one real `useWishlistAuthDrawer`/`ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` instance is expected to live in the step-4.6 container, hoisted above every row. This is disclosed in the component's own docblock (citing the plan's own contradiction, not inventing a precedent). `useCartMessages` — the other half of that same architecture claim — I kept as a direct call, since it's a stateless `useToast()` wrapper with no per-instance cost; that half of the claim checked out.

Both of these are genuine, cited (file:line) conflicts inside the plan/brief itself, not my preference — flagging per your standing instruction rather than silently resolving them.

## Smaller things I found and how I handled them
- No literal precedent exists in this codebase for "other 25px→24px snaps" as the brief claims — I greped and found none (only an unrelated 25px auto-measured-width comment in `zimmBadge.css.ts`). I wrote my own honest snap comment (`zimmCartItemActions.css.ts`) rather than citing a nonexistent example.
- `--zimm-color-link-default` (what `ZimmLink` actually applies) and `--zimm-color-text-default` (what the brief specifies) are different CSS vars but the **same primitive** (`colour.ts:61` and `:87` both resolve to `grey[900]`) — confirmed by reading both definitions, not assumed. So plain `<ZimmLink size="small">` already renders the spec's colour; I did not add a competing colour declaration (would have violated "one canonical styling surface").
- `size="small"` on `ZimmLink` already gives `capitalize` and the 4px vertical padding for free (`zimmLink.css.ts:16,47`) — no extra styling needed for those two requirements either.
- `ZimmLink` carries a real `_hover` and `_focusVisible` (a genuine outline, distinct from default) but **no `_active`** state — pass criterion 2 says "hover, focus-visible, active inherited"; only two of the three actually exist today. Not a blocker (no AC requires a distinct active style), but I didn't assert something that isn't there.
- Used `productId`, not `itemId`, as the resume-matching key in `usePendingWishlistItem` — deliberate: `useCartMergeAndCap.ts`'s own comments confirm a merge can move a line into a new destination basket, which changes `itemId` but not `productId`. Matching on `itemId` would risk silently failing to resume a legitimate pending move right when a merge has just happened.

## Pass criteria — evidence
1. Default styling: `zimmCartItemActions.css.ts` (gap `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, no colour override) + `ZimmLink size="small"` inheriting capitalize/py-4/colour — asserted in `index.test.tsx`'s "default rendering" block.
2. Hover/focus-visible: asserted in `index.test.tsx` directly against `ZimmLink`'s own recipe object (`outline` undefined by default, `_focusVisible.outline` = `var(--zimm-focus-ring)`) — jsdom can't exercise real `:focus-visible` matching, disclosed inline, same limitation `zimmQuantityStepper`'s own tests already accept.
3. No disabled state: no prop exists to request one; `index.test.tsx` asserts neither link ever carries `disabled`/`aria-disabled`.
4/5. Remove: `index.test.tsx` — one call per click, never looped (the callback takes no quantity argument at all, so looping isn't structurally possible from this file).
6. Authenticated success: `index.test.tsx` asserts `onMoveToWishlist` → `onRemove` → `notifyAddedToWishlist(productName)` in that order; `index.stories.tsx`'s `WishlistMoveSuccess` story's `play` asserts the real toast text via `within(document.body)` (portal exception, cited inline) — this also closes step 4.3's own deferred Storybook criterion.
7. Already-in-wishlist: `index.test.tsx` + `AlreadyInWishlist` story — warning message fires, `onRemove` never called.
8. Guest click: `index.test.tsx` — `onGuestWishlistClick` fires, neither `onRemove` nor `onMoveToWishlist` called.
9. Resume from React state: `index.test.tsx`'s cross-render test (same mounted instance, `isGuest` true→false). Resume from session storage after a simulated redirect: `usePendingWishlistItem.test.ts`'s own dedicated test (fresh mount, `isGuest` already false, no prior state).
10. Stale (>5 min) pending item: `usePendingWishlistItem.test.ts` — two tests (storage path and React-state path via `Date.now` mocking) both prove not-resumed-but-cleared.
11. See the two flagged findings above — I did not write new proof for this criterion, per your brief's own instruction; I did decline to write a comment asserting an ordering guarantee I disproved.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (ran twice, before and after all files existed; zero output both times).

## Two things I would not build as literally instructed — both need your ratification, not mine

**1. "Resume fires after merge and cap" (pass criterion 11) rests on a false premise about `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`.**
Consequence: if step 4.6 wires the real SDK calls the way this step's brief describes, a guest's wishlist-move can fire while the guest→registered basket merge is still in flight — the exact "shopper's items are gone" class of bug step 4.1 exists to prevent, just for the wishlist-move path instead of the basket-count path.
Mechanism: I read `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:173-241` directly. `onAuthSuccess?.()` fires **synchronously, before `mergeBasket.mutate(...)` is even called** — not after merge-and-cap resolve as the brief states ("which per steps 4.1/4.2 already fires after merge-and-cap resolve"). `capBasketQuantities(mergedBasket)` only runs later, inside `mergeBasket`'s own `onSuccess`, fire-and-forget, with nothing chained after it. `useCartMergeAndCap.test.ts`'s "sequencing" test (which the brief cites as proof) only proves `capBasketQuantities` itself resolves after its own write settles, using local test-only stand-ins for merge and resume — it does not prove the real `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` actually chains a resume after cap, because it doesn't.
Fix: I wired my resume trigger to `onAuthSuccess` anyway — it's the only signal this step's files have access to, `usePendingWishlistItem`'s own tests pass criteria 9/10 correctly in isolation, and the actual defect only materializes once step 4.6 wires real SDK calls behind `onMoveToWishlist`. I did not write a comment asserting the false "fires after merge and cap" ordering. **Before step 4.6 starts, someone needs to either move the merge-call's resume signal to fire from inside `capBasketQuantities(mergedBasket)`'s own resolution (a `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` change, out of this step's scope) or accept the race and use `productId`-based re-resolution to make it safe regardless (see next point).**

**2. "`ZimmCartItemActions` calling `useWishlistAuthDrawer` directly is correct" contradicts the plan's own cardinality rule.**
Consequence: built as the brief describes, a cart with N items would mount N `useForm`s, 3N `useAuthHelper`s, N `useAuthModal`s and N drawers — exactly the shape the same plan step explicitly rejects two paragraphs earlier ("one `useWishlistAuthDrawer` instance per line item ... untenable against this project's mobile-page-speed priority").
Mechanism: `ZimmCartItemActions` is necessarily rendered once per cart line (supplied into each `product-item`'s own `secondaryActions` slot). The plan requires exactly ONE `useWishlistAuthDrawer` instance for the whole cart (`intentId: 'cart-wishlist'`, singular). A hook call inside a per-row component cannot be "one instance" — I checked whether a conditionally-rendered wrapper could reconcile this (mount the drawer only after the first click) and it doesn't work: `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` needs to wrap the trigger's `onClick` *before* the click happens to intercept it.
Fix: I built `ZimmCartItemActions` to receive `isGuest: boolean` and `onGuestWishlistClick: () => void` as **props**, not by calling the hook itself. The one real `useWishlistAuthDrawer`/`ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` instance is expected to live in the step-4.6 container, hoisted above every row. This is disclosed in the component's own docblock (citing the plan's own contradiction, not inventing a precedent). `useCartMessages` — the other half of that same architecture claim — I kept as a direct call, since it's a stateless `useToast()` wrapper with no per-instance cost; that half of the claim checked out.

Both of these are genuine, cited (file:line) conflicts inside the plan/brief itself, not my preference — flagging per your standing instruction rather than silently resolving them.

## Smaller things I found and how I handled them
- No literal precedent exists in this codebase for "other 25px→24px snaps" as the brief claims — I greped and found none (only an unrelated 25px auto-measured-width comment in `zimmBadge.css.ts`). I wrote my own honest snap comment (`zimmCartItemActions.css.ts`) rather than citing a nonexistent example.
- `--zimm-color-link-default` (what `ZimmLink` actually applies) and `--zimm-color-text-default` (what the brief specifies) are different CSS vars but the **same primitive** (`colour.ts:61` and `:87` both resolve to `grey[900]`) — confirmed by reading both definitions, not assumed. So plain `<ZimmLink size="small">` already renders the spec's colour; I did not add a competing colour declaration (would have violated "one canonical styling surface").
- `size="small"` on `ZimmLink` already gives `capitalize` and the 4px vertical padding for free (`zimmLink.css.ts:16,47`) — no extra styling needed for those two requirements either.
- `ZimmLink` carries a real `_hover` and `_focusVisible` (a genuine outline, distinct from default) but **no `_active`** state — pass criterion 2 says "hover, focus-visible, active inherited"; only two of the three actually exist today. Not a blocker (no AC requires a distinct active style), but I didn't assert something that isn't there.
- Used `productId`, not `itemId`, as the resume-matching key in `usePendingWishlistItem` — deliberate: `useCartMergeAndCap.ts`'s own comments confirm a merge can move a line into a new destination basket, which changes `itemId` but not `productId`. Matching on `itemId` would risk silently failing to resume a legitimate pending move right when a merge has just happened.
